name: Claude Code
summary: Peer agentic repository executor capability for scoped code and documentation work using shared Pipe protocols.

source.notes: Peer executor entry. It must use CLAUDE.md as an adapter and repository protocols as the shared source of truth.

useWhen: A scoped code or documentation ticket has a clear write set and can be isolated from Codex work.
The task benefits from a peer executor and shared handoff protocol.
doNotUseWhen: The ticket touches shared high-risk governance files without serialized ownership.
The task requires GitHub or Linear operations that are unavailable in that Claude Code session.
routing.fallback: Use Codex or the human operator when Claude Code lacks repository state, tool access, or safe write-set ownership.

inputs.name: assignedLinearTicket
inputs.description: Approved ticket with clear scope, expected write set, and handoff expectations.

outputs.name: agentHandoff
outputs.description: Branch, changed files, validation, blockers, and next-step handoff for Codex or human continuation.
outputs.sourceOrDestination: PR, Linear, or repository handoff artifact

schemas.notes: Future multi-agent metrics may normalize Claude Code handoff outputs.

forbiddenOperations: Modify approval gates without explicit scope
Operate on another agent's branch without handoff

risks.description: Parallel executor use can create branch or file conflicts.
risks.mitigation: Require clear write set, branch ownership, and handoff before overlapping work.

governance.dataBoundary: Do not handle secrets, customer data, production data, or private evidence without explicit approval.
governance.sensitiveActionBoundary: Do not weaken AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, approval gates, or multi-agent protocol.
governance.loggingRequirement: Record branch, write set, validations, blockers, and handoff details.
governance.updatePolicy: Update after Claude Code pilot tickets reveal routing or handoff gaps.

review.reviewNotes: Pilot peer-executor entry; use only with clear branch and write-set ownership.

examples.scenario: A small documentation ticket touches a disjoint file.
examples.expectedUse: Use Claude Code when it can follow shared protocols and produce a handoff.
examples.expectedNonUse: Do not assign Claude Code overlapping governance edits while Codex owns the same file set.
